![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14233881/assets/553af60aa28cbdd7565259eacc167187bc9c63a5b30cd78a6c14a3c43603fca2.png)

The scatter plot for the data sets $x$ and $y$ of paired observations and the corresponding linear regression line are shown above.

According to the regression model, what is the residual for the highlighted datapoint?
question.worked_solution:
The residual equals the difference between the actual value of the dependent variable and the value estimated using the linear regression model:

$$
\text{Residual}=\text{Actual}-\text{Estimated}
$$

 

The highlighted datapoint has coordinates $(5,3).$ So, our actual value is $y=3.$

On the other hand, the point on the regression line that corresponds to $x=5$ has the $y$-coordinate $5.$ So, our estimated value of is $\overset{^}{y}=5.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14233881/assets/c558c80b7056b794534146d3b99f399c3084806758f78bd6eddb39e8c89248e9.png)

Therefore, the residual is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Residual} & =\text{Actual}-\text{Estimated} \\  & =y-\overset{^}{y} \\  & =3-5 \\  & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$
